root.label: Chronic Generalized Pruritic Papular Dermatosis with Mucosal Involvement
supporting_facts: erythematous papules, crusts, and fissures on the trunk, upper extremities, and lower lip
scales and fissures on the lower lip
normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
skin biopsy showing spongiosis, erosions, and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate
excluded_candidates: psoriasis: reason ranked lower due to lack of typical scales and distribution
atopic dermatitis: reason ranked lower due to late onset and atypical distribution
salient_findings: scales and fissures on the lower lip
negative phototest for UV-B and visible light

B1.label: Immunologically Mediated Dermatosis
askable_discriminators: Have you experienced any allergies or autoimmune disorders in the past?

B2.label: Photodermatosis
askable_discriminators: Have you noticed any worsening of symptoms with sun exposure?

B3.label: Infectious Dermatosis
askable_discriminators: Have you recently traveled or been exposed to anyone with a similar rash?

askable_discriminators: Have you noticed any new or changing skin growths?

B5.label: Other Dermatosis
askable_discriminators: Have you experienced any other symptoms or conditions that may be related to your skin condition?
requestable_discriminators: Further laboratory tests or specialist referral

static_evidence_items.content: Demographics: white woman in her early 40s
Chief complaint: generalized pruritus of 10-years' duration
Previous treatment: topical corticosteroids with no control of symptoms
Physical examination finding: erythematous papules on the trunk and upper extremities
Physical examination finding: scales and fissures on the lower lip
Laboratory test result: antinuclear antibodies normal
Laboratory test result: urine porphyrin analysis normal
Skin biopsy finding: spongiosis and erosions in the epidermis
Skin biopsy finding: nodular lymphocyte infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis
Skin biopsy finding: peripheral mantle zone surrounding a central germinal center
Skin biopsy finding: cells that were CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative
Phototest result: immediate reading negative for UV-B, UV-A, and visible light
Phototest result: erythema appeared in the area irradiated with UV-A 48 hours afterwards
Figure 1A: Clinical image showing unspecific erythematous papules on the arm
Figure 1B: Clinical image showing scales, crusts, and fissures on the lower lip

Figure 2A: Hematoxylin-eosin staining demonstrates spongiosis and erosions over the epidermis and a nodular infiltrate in the upper and mid dermis composed of lymphoid aggregates with ample germinal centers
Figure 2B: Higher magnification shows the germinal center and mantle of the lymphoid follicles in the dermis
